newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan Housing Bank profits rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Jordan Housing Bank profits rise sharply.

text.p: Jordan Housing Bank's net profits have risen a sharp 58 percent to 7.6 million dinars ($10.7 million) in the first four months of 1997 against the same period last year, bank officials said on Wednesday.
The bank, which is the largest non-government investor in the Amman Financial Market (AMF), attributed its performance to operational and capital gains. Bank officials did not elaborate further.

Banking sources say the bank which plans to double its capital to 50 million dinars soon by a private placement from existing shareholders has secured commitments from Arab investors to participate in the capital rise.
Housing Bank's total assets stood at 1.136 billion dinars by the end of 1996 and its deposits at 918 million dinars.
The bank, Jordan's second largest, has Arab and foreign investors including Kuwait with a 20 percent stake and equal six percent stakes by Oman, Qatar and Iran.

The bank is aggressively expanding its commercial business operations since the government freed it from restrictions it operated under by revoking its licence as a real estate financial institution last April.
